thread:
incident-bot: ENG-433 detected: sustained egress bandwidth saturation in asia-central1 affecting external responses from customer-dedicated pools. Auto-page sent to oncall.

sanjay: seeing the paged alert — high egress out of asia-central across multiple clusters, 95th p50 spike, some 503s. grabbing graphs now.

oncall-anna: I'm on it. can someone drop which customers are on dedicated pools in asia-central1? need to triage customer impact.

marie: list pulled: cust-a, cust-b, cust-c (billing-heavy), and 2 internal test tenants. cust-b shows elevated error rate in their dashboards.

olivia: product: cust-b reported degraded inference latencies in their support ticket just now. They might be in our priority enterprise contract. we should prep customer notification copy.

sanjay: quick metrics snippet:

```
Mon 12:06 UTC - egress bytes: 12.3Gbps (baseline 3.1Gbps)
95th latency (token gen): 650ms -> 1800ms
5xx rate: 0.8% -> 4.6%
KV cache hit ratio: stable
```

sanjay: looks like egress bandwidth / peering is saturated, not model runtime. traceroutes show hops bottleneck at our edge egress gateway in asia-central1.

jordan: net-eng chiming in — we've got peering queue growth on peering-edge-asiaC-01. BGP paths still up. suspected traffic storm from some bursty customers + a backup sync process kicking in.

oncall-anna: Can we mitigate by diverting outgoing egress for non-enterprise tenants to eu-west1 temporarily? what's the risk of routing cross-region traffic for stateful KV caches?

marie: ops note: we can enable per-tenant egress routing override. latency will increase for some traffic but should restore success rates. we need a safe list: keep cust-b in-az but rate-limit them or ask them to switch to dedicated fallback in us-east1.

sanjay: command to apply temporary reroute policy (ops playbook):

```
# ops internal CLI
redwood route-override set --region asia-central1 --match "tenant:non-enterprise" --target-region eu-west1 --ttl 15m --reason "egress saturation"
```

sanjay: will run after approval. needs two approvals from eng-sre + net-eng.

olivia: I'll prep the status page and customer email copy. Draft status page blurb:

```
We are investigating elevated request latency and transient errors for customers in asia-central1. Our engineering team has identified high outgoing egress utilization on the asia-central1 edge and is applying targeted routing adjustments to reduce load while we remediate. You may see increased latency if your traffic is routed via eu-west1 during mitigation. No data loss is expected. Updates to follow.
```

olivia: Customer notification shorter SMS/email copy:

```
Hi — we’re seeing increased inference latency and intermittent errors for services in asia-central1. We’re applying routing changes to restore availability; you may see higher latency briefly. We’ll update in ~30 minutes. — Redwood Status
```

eli: CS: flagged cust-b as priority. I'll open a dedicated channel with their SE and give proactive heads-up once we have the rollback window.

jordan: net-eng approves reroute. i'm +1. note: watch for increased inter-region egress costs and possible rate-limited backpressure on eu-west1 edges.

oncall-anna: eng-sre approve. executing now. I'll watch metrics and keep this thread for comms. running the CLI.

oncall-anna: (running) `redwood route-override set --region asia-central1 --match "tenant:non-enterprise" --target-region eu-west1 --ttl 15m --reason "egress saturation"` — completed, propagation expected ~45s.

sanjay: seeing queue drain on peering-edge-asiaC-01. 5xx rate dropping. good signal.

incident-bot: ENG-433 status update: mitigation in progress (temporary reroute to eu-west1 for non-enterprise tenants). Monitoring for recovery.

olivia: posted status page update + sent targeted email to cust-b with the short copy. added follow-up note for 30min update. copied internal CS channel.

eli: cust-b acknowledged, they appreciate the proactive note. SE asked for ETA to full recovery.

sanjay: next steps: keep reroute in place, monitor 5xx and p95 latency. if stable for 30m, start phased rollback with canary tenants. tech postmortem ticket created: INF-752.

oncall-anna: handing off to sanjay for 0200 UTC rotation. i'll add handoff note in pager duty and leave the reroute in place. ping me if rollback causes issues.

sanjay: taking over. i'll run the 30m check and coordinate rollback plan if good. updating status at +30m.

marie: ops action items saved in incident runbook. cost impacts estimate: +~0.9k USD/hr while reroute active (approx).

incident-bot: ENG-433 update logged. Incident severity remains sev-2. Logs and runbook references: /internal/incidents/ENG-433.

oncall-anna: thanks team. leaving thread to sanjay. :thumbsup:
